{{Top}}
{{Quote|I think something is melting. Free my left leg&mdash;the trouble's near the pelvic servomotor.|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], to [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], aboard the [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref>}}
'''Servomotors''', also called '''servos''', '''intermotors''' or '''movement/balance processors''', were motors used to move mechanical parts, such as bodies of [[Droid/Legends|droids]] or [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] limbs for organic beings. Some vehicles, such as [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Aquatic Terrain Armored Transport]]s, relied on servomotors. Most humanoid droids had a pelvic servomotor to allow them to mimic human movement.

==Description==
Weapons turrets on [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], such as [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]], used servos to rotate.<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

==History==
A "Swimmer" AT-AT stationed on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sedri/Legends|Sedri]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] in the [[Imperial Aquatic Garrison|Sedri aquatic Imperial garrison]] needed a replacement servomotor during the [[Sedri civil war]]. The base's [[Commander/Legends|commander]], [[Aban]], ordered a new motor, which was delivered by [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] along with [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] reinforcements for the base, after which it was installed by technicians. With the servomotor installed, the Swimmer was fully functional and deployed during the [[Battle of Fitsay]]. The vehicle was destroyed during the attack, however, by a group of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] who were aiding the occupants of Fitsay.
